newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks protest at plan to close Islamic schools.
newsitem.headline: Turks protest at plan to close Islamic schools.

text.p: Turks massed in the shadow of Istanbul's historic Blue Mosque on Sunday to protest at a clampdown on Islamic schools ordered by the powerful secularist military.
"We are not here for politics, but for freedom of education," read banners carried by the protestors, mostly supporters of the ruling Islamist Welfare Party.
"Don't touch my Imam Hatips," read others, a reference to state-sponsored Koranic schools threatened by army demands for an anti-Islamist crackdown.

Witnesses said about 100,000 demonstrators filled Sultanahmet square. Women wearing veils and Islamic headscarves were separated from the men in line with Islamist practice. Other protestors perched in treetops waving flags.

The powerful army has ordered compulsory secular education be increased to eight years, fuelling its public row with the government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan -- modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.
Erbakan and his supporters say this will effectively shut the middle section of state religious schools -- known as Imam Hatips -- which start to take pupils at the age of 11.
Turkey's secularists, particularly the military, believe the Imam Hatip schools are used as a breeding ground for activists of Erbakan's Welfare Party.
The eight-year education plan was among demands set out by the military-led National Security Council (NSC) in February.
Erbakan, also a member of the NSC, was a signatory to the council's proposals, but he has been criticised for not implementing them.
Sunday's rally contrasted to one held at the same venue the previous day by the leader of Welfare's pro-Western True Path Party coalition partner, Tansu Ciller.
Some 7,000 of an expected 150,000 people turned up, the Radikal newspaper said, declaring: "The end of Tansu Ciller," in its banner headline.
